title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 18.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 18, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: This event appears first in the chapter, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:1.

questions.question: Who did Jehoshaphat join affinity with?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat joined affinity with Ahab, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:1.

questions.question: What did Ahab do for Jehoshaphat when he went to Samaria?
questions.explanation: Ahab killed sheep and oxen for Jehoshaphat in abundance, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:2.

questions.question: What did Ahab ask Jehoshaphat?
questions.explanation: Ahab asked Jehoshaphat if he would go with him to Ramothgilead, which implies joining his army, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:3.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat request from Ahab?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked Ahab to enquire at the word of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:4.

questions.question: How many prophets did Ahab gather to inquire about the battle?
questions.explanation: Ahab gathered together four hundred prophets to inquire about the battle, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:5.

questions.question: What did all the prophets say to Ahab?
questions.explanation: All the prophets prophesied to Ahab to go up to Ramothgilead and prosper, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:11.

questions.question: Who did Jehoshaphat ask about a prophet of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked Ahab if there was a prophet of the LORD besides the 400 prophets, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:6.

questions.question: What did Ahab think of Micaiah?
questions.explanation: Ahab said he hated Micaiah because he never prophesied good unto him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:7.

questions.question: What did Zedekiah make for the prophets?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah made horns of iron and prophesied that with them they would push Syria until they be consumed, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:10.

questions.question: What did the messenger tell Micaiah to do?
questions.explanation: The messenger urged Micaiah to speak good like the other prophets, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:12.

questions.question: The prophets prophesied that the LORD would deliver Ramothgilead into the king's hand.
questions.explanation: The prophets indeed prophesied that the LORD would deliver Ramothgilead into the king's hand, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:11.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat was king of Israel.
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, not Israel, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:3.

questions.question: Ahab and Jehoshaphat sat on thrones in Samaria.
questions.explanation: Ahab and Jehoshaphat sat on their thrones in a void place at the gate of Samaria, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:9.

questions.question: Micaiah was the prophet who always prophesied good.
questions.explanation: Ahab hated Micaiah because he never prophesied good, but always evil, as stated in 2 Chronicles 18:7.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Micaiah say he would speak?
questions.explanation: Micaiah declared, 'As the LORD liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.' (2 Chronicles 18:13)

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 18:14 promise will happen if Micaiah speaks the truth?
options: They shall be delivered into your hand
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be delivered into your hand
questions.explanation: Micaiah told the king that if he goes up, they shall be delivered into their hand. (2 Chronicles 18:14)

questions.question: How did the king respond to Micaiah's prophecy?
questions.explanation: The king asked Micaiah how many times he must adjure him to speak only the truth, indicating doubt about his sincerity. (2 Chronicles 18:15)

questions.question: What vision did Micaiah recount regarding Israel?
questions.explanation: Micaiah described seeing all Israel scattered upon the mountains as sheep without a shepherd. (2 Chronicles 18:16)

questions.question: What did Ahab say about Micaiah's prophecies?
questions.explanation: Ahab expressed his frustration by stating that Micaiah never prophesied good but always evil. (2 Chronicles 18:17)

questions.question: What did Micaiah see in his vision of the LORD?
options: The LORD sitting on His throne
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD sitting on His throne
questions.explanation: Micaiah saw the LORD sitting upon His throne with all the host of heaven standing beside Him. (2 Chronicles 18:18)

questions.question: What was the purpose of the spirit that came before the LORD?
questions.explanation: The spirit volunteered to entice Ahab so that he would go up and fall at Ramothgilead. (2 Chronicles 18:20)

questions.question: What did the LORD say about the lying spirit?
questions.explanation: The LORD permitted the lying spirit to entice Ahab and said, 'Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail.' (2 Chronicles 18:21)

questions.question: What did Micaiah claim about the prophets of Ahab?
questions.explanation: Micaiah explained that the LORD had put a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab's prophets. (2 Chronicles 18:22)

questions.question: What did Zedekiah do to Micaiah?
options: He smote him upon the cheek
questions.correctAnswer: He smote him upon the cheek
questions.explanation: Zedekiah struck Micaiah on the cheek, questioning the source of Micaiah's prophecy. (2 Chronicles 18:23)

questions.question: What did Micaiah say would happen to Zedekiah?
questions.explanation: Micaiah told Zedekiah that he would see the truth on the day he goes to hide in an inner chamber. (2 Chronicles 18:24)

questions.question: Was Jehoshaphat confident in the prophets Ahab gathered?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat questioned the validity of the prophets' messages and sought a true prophet of the LORD. (2 Chronicles 18:6)

questions.question: Did Ahab have a favorable view of Micaiah?
questions.explanation: Ahab admitted he hated Micaiah because he always prophesied evil against him, showing Ahab's unfavorable view. (2 Chronicles 18:7)

questions.question: Did Micaiah's prophecy align with the majority of the prophets?
questions.explanation: Micaiah's prophecy contradicted the majority who prophesied prosperity for Ahab, indicating his message was not aligned. (2 Chronicles 18:14)

questions.question: Did the prophets encourage Ahab to go to battle?
questions.explanation: The gathered prophets unanimously encouraged Ahab to go up to Ramothgilead, saying that God would deliver it into his hand. (2 Chronicles 18:11)

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 18.

questions.question: To whom did the king of Israel order Micaiah to be taken after his prophecy?
options: Amon the governor of the city and Joash the king's son
questions.correctAnswer: Amon the governor of the city and Joash the king's son
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:25 states that the king of Israel said, 'Take ye Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son.'

questions.question: What kind of bread and water was Micaiah to be fed with in prison according to the king of Israel?
options: Bread of affliction and water of affliction
Bread of plenty and water of refreshment
Bread of leaven and water of bitterness
Bread of mourning and water of sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Bread of affliction and water of affliction
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:26 says the king ordered Micaiah to be fed with 'bread of affliction and with water of affliction.'

questions.question: What did Micaiah say would prove that the LORD had not spoken by him?
options: If the king certainly returned in peace
If the king lost the battle
If the prophets were proven true
If the king was wounded in battle
questions.correctAnswer: If the king certainly returned in peace
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:27 records Micaiah saying, 'If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not the LORD spoken by me.'

questions.question: What disguise strategy did the king of Israel use before going to battle?
options: He disguised himself, while Jehoshaphat wore his robes
Jehoshaphat disguised himself, while the king of Israel wore his robes
questions.correctAnswer: He disguised himself, while Jehoshaphat wore his robes
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:29 states the king of Israel said, 'I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes.'

questions.question: What command did the king of Syria give to his captains of the chariots?
options: Fight only the king of Israel, not small or great
Focus on Jehoshaphat king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Fight only the king of Israel, not small or great
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:30 says the king of Syria commanded, 'Fight ye not with small or great, save only with the king of Israel.'

questions.question: How did Jehoshaphat escape being attacked by the captains of the chariots?
options: He cried out and the LORD helped him, causing them to depart
He disguised himself as the king of Israel
He fled immediately from the battlefield
He was protected by his chariot man
questions.correctAnswer: He cried out and the LORD helped him, causing them to depart
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:31 explains that when captains saw Jehoshaphat, they thought he was the king of Israel, but when he cried out, the LORD helped him and God moved them to depart.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'affliction' (used in 2 Chronicles 18:26) mean?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 18:26, the Hebrew word translated as 'affliction' (עָנִי, 'ani') means suffering or distress, indicating hardship experienced by Micaiah in prison.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 18:18-22 in the depiction of the heavenly council and the lying spirit?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:18-22 describes the LORD sitting on His throne with the host of heaven around Him, a classic example of the divine council literary device portraying a heavenly courtroom scene.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of false prophecy and deceit found in 2 Chronicles 18:21-22?
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:9-12 discusses a lying spirit and deception leading people away from the truth, paralleling the lying spirit placed in the prophets' mouths in 2 Chronicles 18:21-22.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage fulfills the theme of a king being wounded in battle as seen in 2 Chronicles 18:33-34?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 22:34-35 recounts the same event of the king of Israel being wounded and dying in battle, directly paralleling 2 Chronicles 18:33-34.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the king of Israel ordering Micaiah to be imprisoned in 2 Chronicles 18?
options: Micaiah's prophecy about Israel being scattered like sheep without a shepherd
Jehoshaphat agreeing to go to battle
The prophets telling Ahab to go to Ramothgilead
Zedekiah striking Micaiah on the cheek
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah striking Micaiah on the cheek
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:23-24 shows Zedekiah smiting Micaiah, which directly precedes the king's order to imprison Micaiah in verse 25.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 18:27, Micaiah's statement 'If thou certainly return in peace...' serves as what type of literary device?
questions.explanation: Micaiah's statement in 2 Chronicles 18:27 foreshadows the king's death and the falsehood of his prophecy, indicating the outcome contrary to the king's hope.

questions.question: How does the narrative in 2 Chronicles 18:29-34 utilize irony?
options: The king disguises himself but is the one targeted and killed
Jehoshaphat is mistaken for a common soldier
The prophets' good news turns out true
The king of Syria spares the king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The king disguises himself but is the one targeted and killed
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 18:29-34, the king of Israel disguises himself to avoid being targeted, yet a random arrow strikes and kills him, demonstrating situational irony.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Chronicles 18, Jehoshaphat was mistaken for the king of Israel by the Syrians' chariot captains.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:31 states the chariot captains saw Jehoshaphat and said, 'It is the king of Israel,' showing they mistook him for the king.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Israel was killed by a planned and targeted attack by the Syrians according to 2 Chronicles 18.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:33 says a certain man 'drew a bow at a venture' (randomly) and struck the king, indicating it was not a planned, targeted attack.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 18:4 teach about seeking divine guidance?
options: The necessity of enquiring at the word of the LORD before undertaking significant actions
The sufficiency of human wisdom in decision-making
That kings should rely primarily on military advisors
That prophets can be ignored if inconvenient
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of enquiring at the word of the LORD before undertaking significant actions
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:4 shows Jehoshaphat urging Ahab to seek the word of the LORD before going to battle, underscoring the doctrine that divine guidance is necessary before major decisions.

questions.question: What doctrine about the reliability of prophetic testimony is taught in 2 Chronicles 18:7?
options: Not all prophets speak truthfully or beneficially, and some can be rejected
All prophets are equally inspired and trustworthy
Prophetic messages are always encouraging and positive
questions.correctAnswer: Not all prophets speak truthfully or beneficially, and some can be rejected
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:7 reveals Ahab's hatred toward Micaiah because he only prophesied evil, teaching the doctrine that not all prophetic voices are positive or welcome, highlighting the complexity of prophetic authenticity.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's sovereignty in judgment is taught in 2 Chronicles 18:22?
options: God sovereignly ordains even false prophecy to accomplish His purposes
False prophecy exists independently of God's will
God is unaware of human deceit
God cannot use evil for good
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains even false prophecy to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 18:22 states that the LORD put a lying spirit in the mouths of the prophets, teaching that God sovereignly uses even deception to bring about His righteous judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 18:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 18:18, the LORD is depicted sitting on His throne with all heavenly hosts at His sides, showing His supreme sovereignty over all creation and events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 18:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The LORD commands a lying spirit to entice Ahab, showing His absolute sovereignty in orchestrating events, as found in 2 Chronicles 18:21.

questions.question: How does the narrative of 2 Chronicles 18 prepare for themes of divine judgment and human responsibility elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the inevitability of judgment for rejecting God's true prophets, as seen in the prophetic books
It primarily illustrates the success of political alliances
It emphasizes human merit over divine will
It denies the role of prophecy in history
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the inevitability of judgment for rejecting God's true prophets, as seen in the prophetic books
questions.explanation: The chapter’s account of Ahab ignoring Micaiah's true prophecy anticipates broader biblical themes where rejecting God's messengers leads to judgment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 18:16-17 have to the motif of the Shepherd in the Old Testament?
options: It reflects Israel’s need for a true Shepherd, prefiguring Christ
It denies Israel's need for leadership
It teaches that kingship is irrelevant to God’s plan
It asserts that Israel should be scattered without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects Israel’s need for a true Shepherd, prefiguring Christ
questions.explanation: Verse 16’s imagery of Israel as sheep without a shepherd points to the theological need for a messianic shepherd, which is fulfilled in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 18 and 21 teach about God’s control over spiritual beings and human affairs?
options: God exercises sovereign authority even over spirits to accomplish His divine will
God is limited by the actions of spiritual beings
God is unaware of evil spirits’ influence
Human free will overrides divine control
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises sovereign authority even over spirits to accomplish His divine will
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 21 describe how God consults with heavenly hosts and authorizes a lying spirit, showing divine control over spiritual and human realms.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 18:4 and 18:14 teach regarding the role of prophetic revelation in human decision-making?
options: Prophetic revelation must be sought and heeded to align human decisions with God’s will
Prophecy is unreliable and should be ignored
Human wisdom alone suffices for decisions
Prophetic words are always positive and easy to accept
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic revelation must be sought and heeded to align human decisions with God’s will
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat’s insistence to enquire of the LORD (v.4) and Micaiah’s prophecy (v.14) emphasize that seeking and obeying God’s revealed word is essential for proper action.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 18:29 and 18:33 teach about divine providence and human agency in battle?
options: Human actions occur within the framework of divine providence, including unforeseen outcomes
Human strategy alone determines success in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Human actions occur within the framework of divine providence, including unforeseen outcomes
questions.explanation: The king’s disguise (v.29) and his being struck by a random arrow (v.33) illustrate that human choices and chance happen under God’s sovereign plan.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 18:21-22 actually teach about God allowing deception in prophecy, counter to sceptics who claim it undermines God's holiness?
options: God sovereignly permits a lying spirit to accomplish His just judgment, not because He is deceitful but because He controls all things
God endorses falsehood as equal to truth
God is unaware of false prophecy
God’s holiness is compromised by allowing deception
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits a lying spirit to accomplish His just judgment, not because He is deceitful but because He controls all things
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 teach that God uses even a lying spirit to bring about judgment, showing His sovereignty without compromising His holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and divine judgment is taught in 2 Chronicles 18:1?
options: Alliance with ungodly rulers can lead to pride and judgment
Human wealth is a sign of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Alliance with ungodly rulers can lead to pride and judgment
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat’s alliance with Ahab (v.1) exemplifies the theological danger of compromising with unrighteousness, which leads to negative consequences.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 18:27 when Micaiah states the condition for the king's safe return?
questions.explanation: Micaiah’s statement in verse 27 underscores God’s truthfulness in prophecy, affirming that his words reflect God’s genuine message.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 18:30-31 have to the motif of divine protection of the Godly?
options: Jehoshaphat’s deliverance foreshadows God’s protection of His people in spiritual battles
God abandons His people in warfare
Victory depends solely on military strength
God’s protection is arbitrary and uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat’s deliverance foreshadows God’s protection of His people in spiritual battles
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat being spared when mistaken for Ahab (vv.30-31) anticipates God’s providential protection of His faithful in various trials.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 18:6 and 18:12 teach about the challenge of discerning God’s true prophets among many voices?
options: God’s true prophets may be few and unpopular, requiring discernment amidst many false prophets
All prophetic voices are equally valid
Discernment is unnecessary because all prophecy is positive
False prophets are easily recognized and rejected
questions.correctAnswer: God’s true prophets may be few and unpopular, requiring discernment amidst many false prophets
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat’s request for a prophet of the LORD (v.6) and the messenger’s urging Micaiah to conform (v.12) show the difficulty in discerning true prophecy.
